steps.text: Stir milk and vinegar together in a small bowl; allow to stand until curdled, about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking sheet.

Whisk flour, sugar, baking soda, and salt together in a bowl; gradually stir in soured milk until dough just comes together. Turn dough out onto a well-floured surface; knead lightly and shape into a round.
Transfer dough to the prepared baking sheet. Cut an "X" into the top of the dough to release steam and help the bread keep its round shape while baking.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown and the bottom of the loaf sounds hollow when tapped, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Brennan's Irish Soda Bread
raw_recipe.description: This soda bread is made with soured milk, flour, and baking soda for a quick bread with a tender crumb that's always a favorite.

review.reviewBody: Of all the soda bread recipes I've tried , this is by far the best ! I made this for my cafe's St. Paddy's Day luncheon, and the reviews were RAVE ! It even brought tears to one older Irish gent who procliamed " It tasted exactly like his childhood..." Bank on this recipe !

This was delicious! I didn't have high expectations because I had to use gluten free flour and I didn't have any milk so I substituted 1/2 almond milk and 1/2 cream. I made half a batch, divided it into 2 pieces and made 2 very-generously sized mini loaves. I was expecting two little hockey pucks but it raised beautifully and was very tender and moist. This is going to be a go-to recipe in my house.

I made it gluten-free with Bob’s Red Mill 1:1 gluten free flour. I doubled the recipe and added some caraway seeds (1 1/2 tblsp) and 1/2 cup of plumped raisins. Baked for about 55 min since it was a large loaf. It got rave reviews by the GF folks. Will definitely make again.

Delicious! I followed the directions but based on some of the recommendations I added an extra tablespoon of sugar, 2 teaspoons of caraway seeds and half a cup of currents. I baked for 30 minutes. It was absolutely delicious warm with butter.

If you follow the recipe exactly, as I did, the dough comes out too thin. I rescued it by following the Amazingly Easy Irish Soda Bread recipe. I added 2 C of flour, 1/2 C of margarine or butter and 1 egg to the batter. This came out fine. 

In the future I will add 1/2 C of the vinegar and milk mixture and slowly add any additional vinegar and milk mixture until it forms a batter that can be kneaded.

I converted this to be gluten free as I have celiac disease. I used 1 C rice flour, 1 C tapioca, and added 1.5 teaspoons of xanthan gum. I also used a little more salt and a little less sugar. I normally make soda bread when I am too lazy to go buy yeast. This is not the recipe I normally use for soda bread but decided to try this one. It came out very crusty and good.

I have an electric oven, so I put a pan of water on the bottom shelf for moistness. I also baked the bread in a cast iron skillet. Maybe because it was GF, I had to bake it the full 45 minutes. It came out dense, but delicious. I had to exercise self control and not eat the whole loaf.

SO delicious and also easy!!! This was the first time I had ever made Irish soda bread. I added about 1.5 tablespoons of chia seeds and almost 1 cup of craisins to give it a little extra sweetness (and use up some chia seeds).
It only needed to be baked for 30 minutes; 45 would have definitely bben too much in my oven.

This recipe is great! I’ve made it 4 times exactly as written and then began tweaking it for better results. 400F is too hot, so I now bake it at 385F. The time is much too long, so I’ve reduced it to 25 minutes with 15 minutes resting on the baking sheet out of the oven. For the sugar, salt and baking soda I use more generous measurements instead of flat and exact. For the shaping I have found a wide, circular and even disk shape is best. I like to add in a teaspoon or two of caraway seeds, as well. Use all the milk mixture! The dough needs to be wet. In the past I’ve added more flour and got very dense, dry bread.

LOVE this bread! I made it for Saint Patrick’s Day and doubled the recipe! I added raisins to one of them which added a little more sweetness! The dough was a little gooey so I added a few more tablespoons of flour until I could handle it better. I also brushed it with butter and sprinkled sugar on top which gave it a sweet, crunchy crust! It was amazing! Highly recommend!

I usually don't review recipes that I change in any way but all I did differently was to add 1/2 cup of raisins and cut the baking time to 25 minutes(maybe my oven is off or I made my "round"too big). It had the exact texture and just the sweetness I was looking for - moist scone. Delicious. I will be making this again and again.

I have been making this recipe for over 10 years now and at first I was so inexperienced that it came it just ok but as I’ve learned through the years to make bread I realize that the only thing missing in the recipe description is that you need to have a good amount of flour on the table top to knead your dough in since it is wet and sticky. Knead it for 3 mins or when you are able to get it into a round shape and its not sticky on your hands. Scoop it up and place on a parchment paper, cut a cross into the dough and bake. It’s absolutely delicious! By far this is the easiest and best recipe.
very easy and wonderful add to my shepards pie. Next time i am going to go 1/2 rye flour 1/2 reg flour and see how that turns out.

I didn't make any changes but it was a little tough to cut on the bottom crust- but I believe my oven is off. Easy to follow, tasted great and was perfect for soaking up corned beef broth... I will serve it with a big pot of beans, too. My coworkers divided up the leftovers, so I guess it was a success.
I made this when I need a quick bread to go with soup or salad or anything really! So easy!
Thanks for providing an alternative to using buttermilk. My guests and I could not taste any difference. And with such an easy recipe along with good results, who could ask for more?
I made no changes. It was amazing.

This was so easy to make and tasted delicious served warm. I greased a tin pie plate and baked it inside of that- it was the perfect size and worked great. I also brushed a bit of melted butter over the top after I took it out of the oven to make the crust a bit easier to slice (It makes a pretty thick crust) and that was a nice addition for us too.
I used lactose free milk and it didn't rise... was the milk the issue?

I missed the nuance in the instructions, and ended up adding in the whole cup of soured milk at once. This resulted in a wet batter, rather than a kneadable dough. The flavor and texture ended up being more similar to yeast bread than the other soda bread recipes I've made, which have tended to be cake-like; this was a nice surprise. I appreciate that there are no eggs or butter, common allergens and expensive ingredients that aren't always on hand. I'll use this recipe again when I want a quick bread for dinner or sandwiches- doubled, with less liquid, and some herbs or spices.
